newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latin American benefitting from policies - economist.
newsitem.headline: Latin American benefitting from policies - economist.

text.p: Neo-Liberal economic polices coupled with expectations of stable interest rates in the United States have boosted Latin America's economic outlook, said noted economist Rudiger Dornbusch.

Speaking at a conference attended by about 120 investors and government officials, Dornbusch said recent macroeconomic indicators from South American countries have shown average annual growth rates of 6.6 percent.
Dornbusch, who has often criticized government policies in Latin America, said that the neo-Liberal policies have lead him to view the region with "unlimited enthusiasm."
"Everywhere one looks, it looks like Chile, even though not all reforms are in place," Dornbusch, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, said late Wednesday.
The economist said that is was unlikely that the U.S. Federal Reserve would lift interest rates until there was a more widespread increase in prices.
A third element that has supported the constant flow of funds to Latin America is the need for investors to diversify and preserve high yields in their portfolios, he said.
Dornbusch said that Argentina had the best potential for high growth while growth in Chile would continue to accelerate.
He was less enthusiastic about Colombia and Venezuela, and said that although Brazil was an economy with problems, it still offered good perspectives for growth in the next few years.
Dornbusch declined to comment on the situation in Mexico, unlike on earlier occasions when he has roiled financial markets in the country with his statements about monetary policy and the currency.
"I have nothing new to say (about Mexico,)" he told reporters.
